description:
Validate JSON-LD structured data against Schema.org rules and AI-citation best practices. Accepts either a URL (fetched) or a raw JSON string (parsed directly).

Read-only when given `url` (one HTTP GET). Zero network when given `schema_json`. No writes.

Deterministic, rule-based; no LLM. Validates required/recommended properties, @context correctness, sameAs links, and AI-search-friendly patterns.

When to use: focused JSON-LD audits, or to validate a schema block you're about to ship. For a full page audit that includes schema + everything else, use `audit_page` instead.

Either `url` or `schema_json` must be provided (not both). If both are provided, `schema_json` wins and no fetch happens.

respect_robots.description: If true (default), respect robots.txt before fetching `url`. Ignored when `schema_json` is used.

schema_json.description: Raw JSON-LD as a string (the contents of a `<script type="application/ld+json">` block). Use this to validate a schema block offline without fetching a URL. Either this OR `url` is required.

url.description: Public URL to fetch and audit. Either this OR `schema_json` is required. Read-only HTTP GET.

name: audit_schema

ai_citation_readiness_score.description: 0-100 score for the JSON-LD's AI-citation readiness.

category.description: Finding category - which AI-SEO dimension it relates to.

estimated_impact.description: Estimated impact on AI citation probability when resolved.

failure_signal.description: Falsifiability: the observable signal that would prove the fix did NOT work.

leading_indicator.description: Falsifiability: the leading indicator to monitor to confirm the fix is landing.

severity.description: Triage priority: critical blocks AI citation, warning hurts probability, info is nice-to-have.

where.description: Location of the issue (CSS selector, JSON-LD path, robots.txt line, or 'page-level').

found_types.description: Schema.org @type values discovered across all JSON-LD blocks.

title: Audit JSON-LD schema
